description: Insights M3 — introduce a global 7d/30d/90d time-range selector on /insights that re-bases the Signal Summary and all eight chart hooks. Parameterize the six issue-metrics server endpoints + the two agent endpoints to accept a uniform range parameter, reversing the CFD D6 contract and adding a range dimension to agent cost/usage.

tasks.title: Server: range-parameterize the six issue-metrics endpoints (incl. shared MetricsRange type, CFD D6 reversal, quality DTO)
tasks.description: Create the shared `MetricsRange` value type (D1) owning the `7d`/`30d`/`90d` wire vocabulary, day-count map (7/30/90), and null⇒caller-default asymmetry, then add an `int? windowDays` parameter (null⇒today's fixed literal) to the six issue-metrics querier methods — `GetCompletionBucketsAsync`, `GetDeliveryTimesAsync`, `GetStageDurationsAsync`, `GetQualityAsync`, `CumulativeFlowQuerier.GetAsync`, `GetApprovalWaitAsync` — substituting each hard-coded window literal. Bind `string? range` on the six route files, validate presets (unknown⇒400 via the existing `ApiResults.BadRequest` seam), and pass `windowDays` through. Formally reverse the cumulative-flow D6 contract (window becomes range-driven, 90d default on omit; update doc-comments and the `dashboard-cumulative-flow`/CFD spec assertions). Resolve the quality double-window: `Window7d` stays a fixed 7d lens, the range drives the `Window30d` slot + its previous comparison window + the trend span/bucket count, and omit reproduces today's exact shape.
acceptanceCriteria: A `MetricsRange` server type parses/validates exactly `7d`/`30d`/`90d`⇒day counts and maps null/omitted to a null day-count (per-endpoint default); queriers never see the wire string
Each of the six issue-metrics endpoints accepts a `range` query param: `range=90d` drives a 90-day current window (and a same-length previous window for completion/delivery-time/quality)
`range=bad` on any of the six endpoints returns 400
Omitting `range` reproduces today's exact fixed windows (completion-day=30d, completion-week=12w, delivery=30d, stage=30d, quality-primary=30d, cumulative-flow=90d, approval-wait=7d)

Cumulative-flow D6 contract is reversed: window is range-driven with a 90d default; snapshot read path and DTO are unchanged (no new field); doc-comments and CFD spec assertions updated to assert 90d-on-omit AND range-driven otherwise
Quality: `range=90d` makes the primary window 90d, previous 90d, trend 90 buckets, while `Window7d` stays a fixed 7d lens; omit⇒Window7d=7d, primary=30d, previous=30d, trend=30 buckets
Server spec tests (`IssueMetricsApiSpecs` + CFD) cover: range scales window; omit⇒byte-equal today; unknown⇒400; CFD range-driven + 90d-default; quality double-window behavior
Server unit tests pass `windowDays` directly to queriers and assert derived current/previous windows and bucket counts independent of string parsing
`npm test` (server) passes with no regression to existing metric specs
tasks.output: packages/server changes: MetricsRange type + parameterized IssueQuerier/CumulativeFlowQuerier methods + six route bindings + updated CFD doc-comments/specs + green `npm test`
tasks.notes: This task owns the shared MetricsRange type (D1) that T-002 reuses. Per-endpoint back-compat defaults are load-bearing for Dashboard consumers — omit-equality is a hard contract, not a nicety.

tasks.title: Server: range dimension for agent cost and usage (windowed spend + timeseries granularity map)
tasks.description: Add an `int? windowDays` parameter to `AgentSessionQuerier.GetCostWindowedAsync` (substitutes 30-day literals for `windowDays ?? 30` on current+previous; all-time `totalCost`/`todayCost`/`costPerShip` untouched) and `GetUsageTimeseriesAsync` (omit⇒7-day/7-bucket daily). Bind `string? range` on `/agent/cost` and `/agent/usage`, validate presets (unknown⇒400), pass `windowDays` through. Implement the usage bucket-granularity map (D5): `7d`→day(7), `30d`→day(30), `90d`→week(~13); the existing `bucketGranularity` DTO field reports the chosen granularity and the cumulative-cost-per-ship sub-series follows the same bucket grid.
acceptanceCriteria: `/agent/cost` accepts `range`: windowed current+previous spend and per-issue-cost re-base to the range; `totalCost`, `todayCost`, and all-time `costPerShip` are byte-identical with and without a range
`/agent/usage` accepts `range`: timeseries span and buckets re-base to the range
`range=bad` on `/agent/cost` or `/agent/usage` returns 400

Usage granularity map implemented and asserted: 7d⇒day(7 buckets), 30d⇒day(30 buckets), 90d⇒week(~13 buckets); `bucketGranularity` field reports the correct value per range; mapping recorded in design.md (D5)
Omitting `range` reproduces today's behavior: `/agent/cost` windowed = 30d current/previous; `/agent/usage` = 7-day/7-bucket daily
Server spec tests (`AgentCostRollupApiSpecs`/`AgentUsageTimeseriesApiSpecs`) cover: range scales window; all-time figures unaffected; unknown⇒400; omit⇒today; 90d⇒weekly granularity
Server unit tests pass `windowDays` directly and assert cost/usage windows and bucket counts independent of string parsing
`npm test` (server) passes with no regression
tasks.output: packages/server changes: parameterized AgentSessionQuerier cost/usage methods + /agent/cost and /agent/usage route bindings + granularity map + green `npm test`
tasks.notes: Reuses the shared MetricsRange type created in T-001 (D1). Distinct querier seam (AgentSessionQuerier) from the issue-metrics read path, hence a separate task.

tasks.title: Web: global Insights range selector, page-level state, and range threading through all eight chart hooks
tasks.description: Add `type InsightsRange = '7d' | '30d' | '90d'`. `InsightsPage` holds `useState<InsightsRange>('30d')`, renders one selector control (exactly three presets, no from/to picker), and propagates `range` to `SignalSummary` (via the five page-level hook calls) and to `InsightsCharts` (prop) which forwards it to every panel/hook. Each of the eight hooks (`useCompletionThroughput`, `useCompletionTrend`, `useCumulativeFlow`, `useDeliveryTime`, `useStageDuration`, `useQualityMetrics`, `useAgentUsage`, `useCostRollup`) gains an optional `range?: InsightsRange` arg: when present it is appended to the URL (composed with `?bucket=` where both exist) and folded into the `queryKey` tuple (mirroring the existing `'week'` key fold); when absent the URL omits the param and the key keeps its existing shape so Dashboard consumers (`FactoryStatusHeadline`/`AttentionHero`) hit the back-compat branch by construction. `EpicProgressList`/`useEpics` are untouched. M2 window badges already derive from returned `rangeFrom`/`rangeTo` so they re-base for free.
acceptanceCriteria: Insights page renders a selector offering exactly `7d`, `30d`, `90d` with no custom from/to picker, defaulting to `30d` on first load
Changing the selector re-applies the range to the Signal Summary and every chart simultaneously from the single page-level state source

Each of the eight hooks appends `range` to its fetch URL when provided and folds it into `queryKey`; switching range produces a different queryKey (no stale cross-range cache) and issues a fresh request
Each hook's `range` arg is optional: omitting it omits the URL param and preserves the existing queryKey shape (back-compat for Dashboard consumers)
`EpicProgressList` does not receive or react to the range
M2 window badges reflect the selected range's window once fresh data arrives

Web tests (`InsightsPage.test.tsx` + focused hook tests) cover: default 30d; switch invokes hooks with new range; Signal Summary + charts re-render; queryKey isolation across ranges (different keys per range); Dashboard consumers still call shared hooks without a range and pass
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass with no regression
tasks.output: packages/web changes: InsightsRange type + InsightsPage selector/state + range prop-threading to panels + eight hooks (URL+queryKey) + green typecheck and test:run
tasks.notes: Server-first deploy order (design Migration Plan): the server endpoints must accept `range` before the selector is wired, hence the dependency on T-001/T-002. Hooks use mocked responses in tests, but the back-compat contract is enforced server-side.
